requirements.evidence: Every route in the contract is present with the right name, method and middleware (routes/web.php:21-57, including throttle:6,1 on password.email and signed on verification.verify). Login uses email:strict, a lowercase e-mail|IP throttle key, auth.failed/auth.throttle on email, session()->regenerate() and redirectIntended(route('home')) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:35-73). Register uses the str()->transliterate('register|'.$ip) key with 5 attempts, Password::defaults(), Registered, login and regenerate (Register.php:39-78). Password reset rotates remember_token (NewPasswordController.php:37-40). VerifyEmailController returns 403 when the id is tampered (lines 16-18). The locale is pinned in .env.example and phpunit.xml. The reset view has a single name="email" input. Gap: auth/forgot-password, auth/reset-password and auth/verify-email.blade.php are bare <div> fragments with no layout, so these pages are served without <html>/<head>, a title or the Bulma CSS.

conventions.evidence: Named routes and plain wire:model are used throughout, and $fillable comes from the existing #[Fillable]. Deviations: the Livewire components validate with inline arrays ($this->validate([...]) at Login.php:35, Register.php:51) instead of the project's #[Validate] pattern; there is no CHANGELOG/README/docs update even though the conventions require it; the field markup is copied across six forms instead of being extracted into anonymous Blade components; home.blade.php uses @component('layouts.app') rather than an <x-...> component or layout.

security.evidence: Session regeneration on login and register, logout invalidates the session and regenerates the token (LogoutController.php:13-16), forgot-password does not reveal whether the e-mail exists (PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-26), verification checks the id and hash against the logged-in user with hash_equals, both auth components re-check Auth::check() inside submit(), and all output uses {{ }} escaping. Minor issue: layouts/app.blade.php:14 falls back to loading a third-party CDN stylesheet (cdn.jsdelivr.net) without SRI.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/AuthenticationTest.php covers both locales, login success/failure/lockout, register success/confirmed/rate limit, logout, home gating, forgot-password status and the 429 on the 7th request, the single email input, the remember_token rotation, the signed and tampered verification links, and both resend cases. Missing: the Livewire unauthorized-call and tamper tests the conventions require (e.g. an authenticated user calling submit()), invalid or expired reset tokens, strict/unique e-mail rejection on register, and the register page redirecting authenticated users. The hardcoded-URL test uses glob('views/**/*.blade.php'), and PHP glob does not support **, so top-level views such as welcome.blade.php and bulma-test.blade.php are never checked.

simplicity.evidence: VerifyEmailController hand-rolls the id/hash checks that Laravel's native EmailVerificationRequest already provides. Both lang/*/ui.php files define three identical groups ('verify', 'verification', 'email_verification') plus top-level 'verification_sent' and 'email_verification_sent', and only some of these are used. The input/label/error markup is repeated in every form.

readability.evidence: The controllers and components are short and well named. However, the lang files carry dead duplicate keys: verify-email.blade.php uses ui.verify.* while the controller uses ui.verification.sent, and ui.email_verification.*, ui.verification_sent and ui.email_verification_sent are never used. The bulma group also has near-duplicate entries ('working' vs 'working_message', 'card_title' vs 'card_header'). The Pest file calls Event::fake without importing the Event facade and relies on the global alias.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task, and translating welcome/bulma-test follows from the 'all screen text from translation files' requirement. Small extras: the defaults in config/app.php were changed ('Laravel'->'PegaFila', 'en'->'pt_BR'), and a CDN fallback was added to the layout, which the task did not ask for.

issues.explanation: The controller-rendered auth views are bare <div> fragments that never use layouts.app, so these pages are served without an HTML document, title, lang attribute or the Bulma styles.
The Livewire components validate with inline rule arrays instead of the project's mandated #[Validate] attributes on the public properties.

The Livewire security policy requires an unauthorized-call test and a tamper test for each action, and none are present for Login::submit or Register::submit; invalid reset tokens and strict/unique e-mail rejection are also untested.
PHP glob() does not expand **, so the hardcoded-URL check skips the top-level views (welcome, bulma-test, home) that the task explicitly says must be covered.
The conventions require docs and the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section to be updated with the change, and neither is touched.
The verification strings are defined three times plus two top-level aliases, and most of these copies are unused dead keys.
It re-implements the id/hash authorization that Laravel's EmailVerificationRequest already does, which the 'native platform feature' rung of the conventions favours.
The same Bulma field markup (label, control, input, help error) is copied into every form instead of being extracted into an anonymous Blade component.
The layout falls back to loading Bulma from a third-party CDN without subresource integrity, which the task did not ask for.
The config fallback defaults were changed even though the task only asked for .env.example and phpunit.xml.
Event::fake is used without importing Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event and relies on the global facade alias.

review.summary: The change builds the full session-auth flow: Livewire login/register with rate limiting, logout, password reset with remember_token rotation, and tamper-safe e-mail verification, with pt_BR translations and a broad Pest suite, and it meets nearly every functional requirement and route contract. However, the three controller-rendered auth pages have no layout, the Livewire components skip the project's #[Validate] convention, the required Livewire unauthorized/tamper tests are missing, the hardcoded-URL test never checks top-level views, the lang files carry duplicate dead keys, and docs/CHANGELOG are not updated, so it needs changes before merging.
